The History of Persia
§B(FLAVOR DECISION)§! Learn more about the history of Persia.

The Persian Empire was one of the most powerful and influential states in the middle east for the last 100 years. They were the ones to invite the turkic raiders to settle in Syria, establishing a Persian vassal state there, and led to the end of Cappadocias domination of the Asia Minor region. Persia did however end up experiencing major political instability, partly due to the wars with the Rashidun, Egyptians, and Armenians, partly due to overextension and partly due to a weak emperor. The Sultanate of Rum declared independence once the third Rum-Cappadocian war was finished, using their new lands to defeat the Persian armies. When the Persian Emperor died his heir was still a young child, leading to a power struggle that escalated into a fullblown civil war. The two remaining factions are the Shia Insurrection, who wish for a more religious orientation with regards to governance, and the Safavid dynasty, led by Persian general to install himself on the throne. The future of the Empire hangs in the balance.
The History of Rum
§B(FLAVOR DECISION)§! Learn more about the history of Rum.

The lands of Syria were taken from the Greeks by the Persians in the 5th greco-persian war during the late 17th century. To administer the land and ensure the population was loyal, the Persian Emperor elevated his most loyal Turkic cavalry to the status of nobility, and gave them the lands in Syria to rule and administer in his name. The Sultanate of Rum then administered these lands as a vassal faithfully, serving as a valuable ally in the many wars against Cappadocia. However, as the situation in Persia became more and more unstable they lost their appetite for war, and instead sought to have long lasting peace with the Greeks. Rum, being only able to govern a small region in the Levant, was not supportive of this and started a war in 1794 to seize parts of Eastern Anatolia. They won, seizing the lands which gives Cappadocia its name, without the help of Persia, which eventually led to them declaring their independence in 1808.

The nation has had a long line of great monarchs which will weigh heavily on the recently crowned Osman II, his grandfather Mehmed III oversaw the creation of the fierce army of Rum and won several wars against the Greeks, Osman's father Suleiman II achieved independence and built a strong nation. In an attempt to create his own long lasting legacy, Osman II has set his eyes on the prize that no other Sultan has been able to claim: Anatolia. To expel the Greeks from the Middle East was the one dream of Mehmed III that he could never achieve, and Osman's father considered it too ambitious. Yet with the army his grandfather built and the state his father refined, Osman II has seen an opening with the Greek famine of 1824 and aims to finally conquer the lands of Central Anatolia.
The History of Egypt
§B(FLAVOR DECISION)§! Learn more about the history of Egypt.

The Egyptian Sultanate is a nation in crisis. Due to the many rebellions during the late 18th century, the already weak Sultan had to give even more power to the many factions within Egyptian politics to secure his dynasty as the continued rulers of Egypt. This has led to the nation essentially being in a perpetual deadlock, with the many factions vying for power and the Sultan's nonexistant power leading to the Sultanate being unable to adapt to the times. A once shining beacon of civilization during era of classical antiquity, a leader during the crusades, and powerbroker during the 17th and 18th century has now been reduced to a slowly decaying carcass, bound to be subjugated by a foreign invader. The commoners speak of the Sultan as a modern Akhenaton in hushed tones, the Egyptian Pharoh who threw Egypt into chaos with his wild reforms.
The History of Armenia
§B(FLAVOR DECISION)§! Learn more about the history of Armenia.

The Kingdom of Armenia is one of the longest lasting states in the entire world. Having served as a valuable ally against the Parthians during the times of Rome, today they serve a similar role. Armenia has the title 'Guardian of Christendom', a fair title since they have valiantly defended the Christians of the middle east from being subjugated and converted for nearly a millennium. As a staunch ally of the Cappadocians, Armenia has kept the Persian Empire at bay for the last 200 years of the Persian golden age. With the outbreak of the Persian Civil War many had hoped that this would lead to continued stability in the Christian East, yet this dream was crushed when Turkic armies once more marched into Anatolia. Additionally many of the ambitious statements made by king Philip VIII of Cappadocia has led to a deterioration in the relationship between the Greeks and Armenians. The future of the ancient nation is uncertain, and they will have to adapt to these new circumstances with haste.
The History of Afghanistan
§B(FLAVOR DECISION)§! Learn more about the history of Afghanistan.

The Kingdom of Afghanistan is an oft-overlooked nation with a proud history. Situated inbetween the Persian Empire, or atleast the remains of it, and the lands of Hindustan, Afghanistan has served as a valuable buffer state for both lands. The nation is however experiencing turmoil. People worry that the outcome of the Persian Civil War could result in a government less willing to to leave us be, and to the North a mighty general has forged a new Khanate, hellbent on seeing the world kneel before him. The nobility in Afghanistan still cling to their ancient greek ancestry, while the majority of the population see themselves as devout muslims. This identity crisis needs to be resolved if the nation seeks to continue existing.
The History of the Rashidun
§B(FLAVOR DECISION)§! Learn more about the history of the Rashidun Caliphate.

The Rashidun Caliphate, ruled by the Caliph of Mecca, is the steward of the Islamic faith and provides guidance to all it's followers. Trouble arose during the many conflicts of the 9th and 10th centuries, the Caliphate was overextended and unable to support many key conflicts, leading to 1704 when the Sultan of Al-Andalus claimed the title of Caliph and established the Umayyad Caliphate. Soon after the Rifians gained independence, they likewise established their own caliphate in 1782. The Islamic world has fractured, and we are left to pick up the scattered pieces.
